Detect the language of states

Source: R/text.R
laya_detect_language.Rd

Reads each state's text (string values only; keys are ignored) and reports its dominant script, a best-effort language guess for Latin-script text, and whether the English checkpoint can read it. Use it to pick a checkpoint: "english" when is_english is TRUE, "multilingual" otherwise. No model is needed.

Usage

laya_detect_language(states)

Arguments

states

A character vector of texts, a single state (a named list), a list of states, or a data frame (one state per row).

Value

A data frame with one row per state and columns script, language (an ISO 639-1 code, or NA when undecided or not Latin), is_english, language_undecided, diacritic_rate, non_latin_fraction, mixed_segment and script_profile (a list-column of named numeric vectors: the share of letters in each script).

Details

A structured state that reads English as a whole is also checked field by field and line by line, so a short message in another language next to a long English stack trace still counts as non-English (mixed_segment shows the part that decided it).

Examples

laya_detect_language(c(
  "Please refund the duplicate charge",
  "मार्च का बिल दो बार लिया गया",
  "glömt lösenord"
))
#>       script language is_english language_undecided diacritic_rate
#> 1      latin       en       TRUE              FALSE         0.0000
#> 2 devanagari     <NA>      FALSE               TRUE         0.0000
#> 3      latin       sv      FALSE              FALSE         0.1429
#>   non_latin_fraction mixed_segment script_profile
#> 1                  0          <NA>              1
#> 2                  1          <NA>              1
#> 3                  0          <NA>              1
laya_detect_language(list(
  subject = "Refund",
  body = "Hola, me cobraron dos veces. \u00bfPueden devolverme el dinero?"
))
#>   script language is_english language_undecided diacritic_rate
#> 1  latin       es      FALSE              FALSE              0
#>   non_latin_fraction mixed_segment script_profile
#> 1                  0          <NA>              1
